title: Thanksgiving Leftovers Recipe Roundup
contentHtml:
Thanksgiving Day is only the beginning—the race to use up those leftovers is about to begin!

Thanksgiving leftovers are arguably as iconic as the Turkey Day meal itself. Spanning cuisines, flavor profiles, and applications, we've gathered our most creative ways to use up those leftovers with a particular emphasis on how to work through lots of leftover turkey meat. Dive in!

These pot pies are warm and koji!

Turkey Leftovers: Freestyle

From our "Warm & Koji" Thanksgiving series, these Japanese curry pot pies use up leftover meat and vegetables while tasting like something entirely their own. Have leftover puff pastry? Even better! Try it out yourself: Japanese Curry Pot Pies. 🔗

Turkey soup is a classic move for the days after Thanksgiving—just be sure not to toss the turkey carcass beforehand! Leftover Roast Turkey Soup. 🔗

Another soup option is this paitan-style broth ramen that cooks at a low rolling boil, resulting in a rich, deep brown stock that is loaded with turkey flavor: Turkey Paitan Ramen With Crispy Turkey and Soft-Cooked Egg Recipe. 🔗

The Hot Brown is a broiled, sauce-covered turkey sandwich that gives your thicker cuts of leftover turkey a much-deserved second life: The Kentucky Hot Brown. 🔗

Break away from the traditional Thanksgiving flavor palate with a "Ragin' Roman," a hot sandwich flavored with Calabrian chile mayo and broiled radicchio: Hot Turkey Sandwiches with Chili Mayo and Roasted Radicchio. 🔗

In the first days after Thanksgiving, leftovers are a breeze. It's all turkey soup, sunshine, and rainbows. A few days later, it becomes more of a chore. Enter mysterious-flavor turkey, based on the Sichuan "guaiwei." One of my all-time favorite treatments for cooked poultry, this brings new flavors to the floor: Bang Bang Ji Si. 🔗

Tom Yum Nam Khon, the creamy version of Thailand’s classic hot-and-sour Tom Yum soup, is simple to make while packing in complex flavors: Leftover Turkey Tom Yum Nam Khon. 🔗

These turkey n' dumplings feature biscuit-like dumplings (with an egg to help them puff as they simmer) and a rich, creamy broth. This is also the perfect place to utilize some leftover gravy: Turkey and Dumplings. 🔗

Another place to use up some leftover gravy is as a dip for these turkey grilled cheese sandwiches: Thanksgiving Leftovers Grilled Cheese Recipe. 🔗

Take all the leftovers you got, wrap them in store-bought pizza dough, and bring them to a piping-hot, Hot Pocket life. Check out the recipe from NYT Cooking (paywalled): Thanksgiving Leftovers Hot Pockets. 🔗

Crispy-edged green enchiladas.

Turkey Leftovers: In Tortillas

Turns out, we turn to tortillas quite often at JKLA World HQ to sort out turkey leftovers. So often, in fact, there are six recipes to share doing just that! First up, we have some green enchiladas. This recipe is forgiving of whatever state your turkey meat might be in. Smother it in sauce and give it a try: Leftover Turkey Green Enchiladas (Crispy-Edge Style). 🔗

Next, we have two takes on quesadillas. These quesadillas combine turkey and black beans for a quick snack: Roast Turkey and Black Bean Quesadillas Recipe. 🔗

While these quesadillas introduce charred, nutty Brussels sprouts to gooey, melted cheese. It's a match made in leftovers heaven: Easy Turkey and Brussels Sprout Quesadillas Recipe. 🔗

For the third recipe bringing together turkey and tortillas, we're making "carnitas." In other words, turning leftover turkey meat into wonderfully crispy and juicy taco filling: Leftover Turkey "Carnitas." 🔗

Did you know there were fully-domesticated turkeys in Mexico well before the 16th century? There's a reason turkey goes so well with this cuisine! For the fourth recipe here, an easy stove-top method delivers tasty results in just 15 minutes with a complex mole sauce: 15-Minute Turkey Enchiladas Recipe. 🔗

Finally, you can see how well turkey and chiles go together in this bowl of tortilla soup. Depending on your chosen toppings, this soup can range from soft, warming, and creamy to fresh, acidic, and zingy: Turkey Tortilla Soup Recipe. 🔗

These pancakes bring a second life to sweet potatoes.

Other Thanksgiving Leftovers

Keeping with the tortilla theme—though without the turkey—these quesadillas replace cheese with sweet potato and are still delicious. Trust the process: Cheese-Free Sweet Potato "Quesadillas" Recipe. 🔗

We've said it before, we'll say it again: Waffle your leftovers! A waffle iron is the perfect tool for revamping your leftover stuffing, maximizing crispy edges and building tiny pools for gravy: Stuffing Waffles Recipe. 🔗

You can take it a step further with a French-style croque madame sandwich over a leftover stuffing waffle: Turkey and Stuffing Waffle Croque-Madame Sandwich Recipe. 🔗

And if you have leftover mashed sweet potatoes, these pancakes put them in an entirely new light: Sweet Potato Pancakes Made With Leftover Mashed Sweet Potatoes Recipe. 🔗
